summary: Genesis names Zeboiim alongside Sodom, Gomorrah and Admah in its description of the Canaanite boundary. It later names a king of Zeboiim.

senses.definition: The city ruled by Shemeber and named alongside Admah in the description of the Canaanite boundary.

evidence.note: Zeboiim, spelled צְבֹיִם with one yod, follows Admah in the list of places along the boundary.
Shemeber’s title מֶלֶךְ צְבוֹיִים, “king of Zeboiim,” parallels Shinab’s title מֶלֶךְ אַדְמָה, “king of Admah.”
The phrase וּמֶלֶךְ צְבוֹיִם names the city ruled by the fourth king in the list. Here the name has a single yod where צְבוֹיִים in Genesis 14:2 has two.
